units.text: Om! — This syllable is this whole world Its further explanation is: — The past, the present, the future — everything is just the word Om And whatever else that transcends threefold time — that, too, is just the word Om,
For truly, everything here is Brahma; this self {diman) is Brahma. This same self has four fourths. (b) representing in its phonetic elements the four states of the Self
The waking state {jdgmnta-sihdnci) outwardly cognitive having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the gross {sthtda-bhuj) the Common-to-all-men {vaisvdnara) is the first fourth.

The dreaming state {svapna-sthdnd) inwardly cognitive having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the exquisite {pravivikta-bhuj) the Brilliant {taijasd) is the second fourth. Inasmuch as aksaram means also ‘ imperishable,’ the word may in this connection be used with a double significance, namely, This imperishable syllable

If one asleep desires no desire whatsoever, sees no dream whatsoever, that is deep sleep [sustipta). The deep-sleep state {susupta-sthana) unified {eM-bhuia)p just a cognition-mass (prajnma-ghana)p consisting of bliss {dnanda-mayd)p enjoying bliss {ananda-bhuj), whose mouth is thought {ceias-) the Cognitional {prdjria), is the third fourth.

This is the lord of all {sarvesvard)P This is the all knowing {sarva-jBa)P This is the inner controller (antarymnin)P This is the source {yoni) of all, for this is the origin and the end {prabhavdpyayau) of beings.

Not inwardly cognitive {antah-prajna) not outwardly cognitive {bahih-prajna), not both- wise cognitive prajna\ not a cognition-mass {prajndna-gJiana\ not cognitive (prajm), not non-cognitive (a-prajnd) unseen (a-drsfa), with which there can be no dealing {a-vyavahdrya\ ungraspable grdhyd) having no distinctive mark {a 4 aksana) non-thinkable {a-cintyd), that cannot be designated {a-vyapadesya) the essence of the assurance of which is the state of being one with the {ekdtmya-pratyaya-sdra\ the cessation of development {prapancopasama\ tranquil {sdnia\ benign {sivd) without a second (-zW)-[such] they think is the fourth. He is the Self (Atman). He should be discerned.
This is the Self with regard to the word Om with regard to its elements. The elements \mdtrd) are the fourths; The part of the sentence tip to this point has occurred already in Brih, 4. 3. 19.

The waking state, the Common-to-all-men, is the letter the first element, from apti obtaining) or from adimatva {' being first He obtains, verily, indeed, all desires, he becomes first — he who knows this.

The sleeping state, the Brilliant, is the letter the second element, from titkarsa (‘exaltation’) or from tibhayaiva (‘intermediateness’). He exalts, verily, indeed, the continuity of knowledge; and he becomes equaP {samdna)\ no one ignorant of Brahma is born in the family of him who knows this.

The deep- sleep state, the Cognitional, is the letter the third element, from miti (‘erecting’) or ixom aplti (‘ immerging He, veril}/, indeed, erects {minoti) this whole world, and he becomes its immerging — he who knows this.

The fourth is without an element, with which there can be no dealing, the cessation of development, benign, without a second. Thus Om is the Self (Atman) indeed. He who knows this, with his self enters the Self — yea, he who knows this!
